objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with sudden, unilateral loss of vision.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: About 30 minutes ago, I suddenly lost vision in my right eye while I was watching TV—there’s no pain, and it’s painless and sudden. My left eye feels normal, and I haven’t had any trauma.

Do you have any weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, facial droop, or trouble walking right now?
Do you have any weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, facial droop, or trouble walking right now?
“No—right now I don’t feel any weakness or numbness, and I’m not having trouble speaking, no facial droop, and I can walk normally.”
Did the vision loss affect the entire right eye or only part of it, and was it completely black/dark versus blurry or like a curtain coming down?
“It feels like a curtain came down over part of my right eye, and the vision turned dark/blocked rather than just blurry. It wasn’t the whole eye at once, more like a section of it.”
Have you had any headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, fever, or recent weight loss?
“No, I don’t have any headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, fever, or recent weight loss.”
Any flashing lights, new floaters, or a sensation of a shadow spreading across your vision before or during this?

“No, I didn’t notice any flashing lights or new floaters, and I didn’t really have a shadow spreading gradually—rather it was sudden and then the curtain/blocking stayed over that part of my right vision.”
Do you have a history of high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, smoking, atrial fibrillation, prior stroke/TIA, or carotid artery disease?

“Yes—I have high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, I smoke about 10 cigarettes a day, and I have coronary artery disease. I’m not sure about high cholesterol, and I don’t recall having atrial fibrillation or a prior stroke/TIA.”
[DDX] Branch retinal artery occlusion, Amaurosis fugax from carotid/cardiac embolus, Central retinal artery occlusion, Retinal vein occlusion, Retinal detachment
